n11.point: The '294 Patent reduces undesirable gate leakage in GaN FET transistors by making the GaN gate less conductive (more insulating), termed a 'compensated' GaN gate layer.
n11.quote: this undesirable gate leakage is reduced by making the GaN gate less conductive of electricity (i.e., more insulating), which is termed a "compensated" GaN gate layer.

n12.point: The '508 Patent describes a self-aligned single-mask gate manufacturing process for enhancement-mode GaN transistors, improving upon traditional multi-mask processes that resulted in gate misalignment, wider gate length, higher gate charge, higher on-resistance, and higher manufacturing costs.
n12.quote: the self-aligned (single mask) process of the '508 Patent results in enhancement mode GaN transistors with significantly improved performance and lower cost.

n13.point: The '347 Patent relates to methods of manufacturing GaN FETs with reduced gate leakage using a self-aligned manufacturing process resulting in a gate structure with a pair of ledges on the upper surface to reduce gate leakage along the gate structure periphery.
n13.quote: the inventors of the '347 Patent developed a novel and non-obvious self-aligned manufacturing process that results in a gate structure with a pair of ledges on the upper surface of the gate structure.

n14.point: The '335 Patent relates to GaN FETs with reduced gate leakage current featuring a gate structure with a pair of self-aligned ledges of substantially equal widths on the upper surface of the gate material.
n14.quote: the inventors of the '335 Patent developed a novel and non-obvious GaN FET having a gate structure with a pair of self-aligned ledges of substantially equal widths on the upper surface of the gate material.

about.text: Complainant Efficient Power Conversion Corporation (EPC) is a California-based company that researches, designs, manufactures, and sells gallium nitride (GaN) semiconductor devices, a technology said to offer higher efficiency, smaller size, and lower cost than older silicon-based transistors. The named respondents are Innoscience (Zhuhai) Technology Company, Ltd., a Chinese manufacturer, and its U.S. affiliate Innoscience America, Inc. of Santa Clara, California. EPC's products are enhancement-mode GaN transistors, a type that stays off unless voltage is applied, which EPC says are safer and more controllable than earlier depletion-mode designs, and are built on inexpensive silicon substrates (GaN-on-Si) so they can be made in existing factories.

EPC asserts four U.S. patents: the '294 patent, covering a 'compensated' gate layer that reduces current leakage; the '508 patent, covering a self-aligned, single-mask manufacturing process for the transistor gate; the '347 patent, and the '335 patent, both covering a gate structure with self-aligned 'ledges' that further reduce leakage. The accused products are GaN-on-Si transistors, high electron mobility transistors, and related components such as bidirectional transistors, multichip modules, and demo boards sold by Innoscience. The Commission instituted the investigation to determine whether importing and selling these products violates Section 337, a trade statute barring unfair imports, based on alleged infringement of specific claims (numbered elements defining the scope of a patent) of the four patents.

allegations.text: EPC alleges that Innoscience's products entered the United States, pointing to a March 2023 shipment from Innoscience's Chinese manufacturing arm that arrived at a purchaser's address in New York after being ordered through Innoscience America's local representative. EPC further alleges that specific Innoscience products, identified as INN650DA140A and INN100W032A, directly infringe the asserted patents' claims either literally or under the doctrine of equivalents (a way of finding infringement even without an exact literal match), and that some of these products are made using processes that themselves infringe the patented manufacturing methods.

To bring a Section 337 case, a complainant must show a 'domestic industry'—its own qualifying U.S. activity tied to the patented technology. EPC alleges this requirement is met through its significant U.S. investment in plant, equipment, research and development, engineering, and other functions, with about 72% of its U.S. workforce tied to products practicing the asserted patents, including representative transistors EPC2016C and EPC2215.

EPC also alleges related misconduct, claiming that two former EPC employees who had access to proprietary technical and customer information later joined Innoscience in senior technical and sales roles, and that Innoscience publicly touted GaN products with 'pin-to-pin compatibility' with EPC's patented products while announcing plans to expand into U.S. markets.

EPC asks the Commission for a limited exclusion order (a bar on importing the infringing products, as opposed to a broader order covering an entire industry) against Innoscience and its affiliates, permanent cease and desist orders barring further sale, marketing, and distribution of the accused products in the United States, and a bond during the 60-day period in which the President may review any Commission remedy.

answers.text: Innoscience denies infringing any claim of the asserted patents and denies committing any unfair acts, and disputes that EPC has a qualifying domestic industry under Section 337. Innoscience raises prosecution history estoppel, arguing that statements and amendments EPC's patent owners made to the Patent Office during prosecution bar EPC from now asserting infringement under the doctrine of equivalents or adopting contrary claim interpretations. Innoscience also alleges inequitable conduct and unenforceability, contending that inventor Dr. Beach withheld his own prior patents and publications material to patentability during prosecution of the '294 and '508 patents, and that EPC's patent counsel misrepresented to the Patent Office that a delay in claiming priority to earlier applications was 'unintentional' in order to overcome a prior-art rejection affecting the '347 and, derivatively, the '335 patents. Innoscience further argues that the exclusion and cease and desist relief EPC seeks would harm the public interest, competitive conditions, and U.S. production of competing articles, and asks the Commission to find no violation, declare the patents invalid and unenforceable, and terminate the investigation.
answers.who: Innoscience (Zhuhai) Technology Company, Ltd. and Innoscience America, Inc.

summary.headline: Efficient Power Conversion Corporation (EPC) accuses Innoscience (Zhuhai) Technology Company, Ltd. and its U.S. affiliate Innoscience America, Inc. of importing and selling gallium nitride (GaN) semiconductor transistors and related products that infringe four EPC patents on GaN transistor structures and manufacturing methods.
